items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: That was one of my original musicians from Birmingham, Alabama, and he was with my Collegians

ctx.x: Yes. In transferring to Wilberforce University in Ohio, which is right out of a little town called Xenia, Ohio, my brother at that time was playing in New York City at (Unintelligible) the Roseland Ball Room at 51st and Broadway. And he used to send me arrangements, piano parts of things, and of course, I have to bring Fletcher into these things because it borders on answering (inaudible) your questions. Fletcher had a band that was uncanny in playing arrangements and memorizing them

quick. And as soon as they would memorize these arrangements, Fletcher would take them up and send them to me. And I -- this was at Wilberforce University -- and I would study these things, and I found out that the people that recommended this particular school to me were so right in saying that there were a lot of musicians that went to Wilberforce. So this is where I found my band called the Wilberforce Collegians, and we sounded horrible. Nobody knew anything about intonation. The guys could read. A lot of…
